descriptionChirho: Qal stem denoting intransitive passing or passing away, used of time, decrees, or states ceasing to exist. Multilingual evidence converges: Spanish 'paso/pasara/puede ser revocada,' Hindi 'tulti/hatega,' Arabic 'tulga/yazulu/tamurra,' Korean 'pyehal/jinaganeun,' Swahili 'pita/batilishwe.' All Qal forms share this intransitive sense of something passing, elapsing, or being annulled.

Hifil causative stem indicating active removal or taking away of authority, dominion, or status by an external agent. Spanish 'le quitaron/quitaran/quita,' Hindi 'hata di gayi/hataenge/hatata hai,' Arabic 'uzila/yuziluna/muzilu,' Korean 'jegeo-doeotda/jegeohal geosida,' Swahili 'uliondolewa/wataondoa/anawaondoa.' The causative Hifil clearly distinguishes this from the intransitive Qal passing.
